In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Ha-Mim. By the Manifest Book﴾. That is: the Book in which the lawful and the unlawful are made clear, and the reward and the punishment, and the promise and the threat.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surah Ha-Mim al-Dukhan (Surah 44)

It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Ha-Mim. By the Manifest Book﴾. That is: the Book in which the lawful and the unlawful are made clear, and the reward and the punishment, and the promise and the threat.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 3:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾, has two interpretations. The first: it is the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr). This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

The second view is that of 'Ikrimah, namely that it is the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban (Laylat al-Nisf min Sha'ban). He called it blessed because of the abundance of good in it. Barakah (blessing) is the growth of good, and its opposite, shu'm (ill omen), is the growth of evil. It has also been said that it is called blessed because the answering of supplication is hoped for in it.

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, We sent it down﴾, the reference is to the Qur'an. Regarding the meaning of this sending down, there are two views. The first: the entire Qur'an was sent down in the Night of Decree to the lowest heaven (al-sama' al-dunya), and then Jibril (peace be upon him) would bring it piece by piece until all of it had been revealed.

The second view: what is meant by the sending down here is the commencement of the revelation.

The meaning of His saying, ﴿We sent it down﴾, i.e., We began its revelation in the Night of Decree.

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, We have always been warners﴾, i.e., We have been those who warn (munDhirin).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 4:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿In it every wise matter is made distinct﴾. That is, every firmly decreed matter is decided, and that includes provisions, lifespans, life and death, and good and evil. Mujahid said: except happiness and misery, for these two are not changed or altered. And it is related from some of them: except death and life as well. And in the tafsir it is stated that He distinguishes the rulings in this night until the coming year, at this night.

"And His saying: ﴿a command from Us﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar), as if He had said: "He separates [every matter] with a separating," then He placed amran (a command) in the place of His saying: farqan (a separating).

And His saying: ﴿from Us. Indeed We have been senders﴾ means: sending down these matters."

Allah's words: ﴿A mercy from your Lord﴾, meaning: the sending down of the Qur'an is a mercy from your Lord.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, the meaning is apparent.

The Almighty's words: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾. It has been recited as "Lord of the heavens" (رب السَّمَوَات). As for "rabbu" (رَبُّ) with a damma on the ba', it is a conjunction ('atf) on His words ﴿He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. As for "rabbi" (رَبِّ) with a kasra, it is a substitution (badal) for His words ﴿from your Lord﴾.

His words ﴿[and what is between them] if you are certain﴾: certainty (al-yaqin) is the calm and settling of the breast upon what one knows.
God's words, the Exalted: ﴿There is no god but Him; He gives life and causes death, your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers.﴾ Meaning: "the earlier ones," that is, those who came before.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on Surah 44, verse 9:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, but they are in doubt, playing.﴾ That is: they listen as one who plays listens, they speak as one who plays speaks, and they accept as one who plays accepts.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So watch for the day when the sky brings forth a manifest smoke﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: This smoke is in this world. That is because the Prophet (ﷺ) invoked against the disbelievers of Mudar, and said: "O Allah, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, and make it upon them as years like the years of Joseph." So they were struck by famine and severe drought, and the land became barren until they ate the bones and carrion. A man among them would look up at the sky and see between himself and the sky something like smoke, from hunger. It is narrated that Abu Sufyan came to the Prophet and said: "O Muhammad, you have invoked against your people, meaning Quraysh, and they are only your brothers, uncles, maternal aunts and paternal aunts. So pray for them." He prayed for them, and they were given rain.

It is also narrated that he (Abu Sufyan) was sent with gold to the poor of Makkah, until he distributed it among them.

The second opinion: the smoke will occur on the Day of Resurrection. This is the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah, and it has been said: it is the more sound (al-asahh). In the tafsir: people on the Day of Resurrection will be seized by something like smoke. As for the believers, it will afflict them like a cold, while as for the disbelievers, the smoke will enter their ears and nostrils, and their heads will become like domes (al-janabidh). It has also been said: the smoke is one of the signs of the Hour. In some reports: "Hasten to good deeds before six: the rising of the sun from its west, the smoke, the beast, the Dajjal, the особый matter of a person himself, and the matter of the common people." The meaning of "the particular matter of a person himself" is death, and the meaning of "the matter of the common people" is the Resurrection. Ibn Mas'ud used to say: five have already passed: the smoke, the blood, the moon, the striking (al-batshah), and the clinging (al-lizam).
"The saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿It will envelop the people; this is a painful punishment﴾. That is: painful (mu'lim)."
"His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, remove the punishment from us; indeed we are believers﴾. That is: we will believe in Muhammad if You remove it. It is a report of the disbelievers."

Divine saying, the Exalted: ﴿How can they have the reminder, when there has come to them a manifest Messenger?﴾ Its meaning: remembrance and admonition. And His saying ﴿manifest﴾ means: clarifying. ﴿Anna﴾ (how, in what way) means: "how?"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then they turned away from him and said: "One taught (by others), a madman."﴾ The meaning: how can they be admonished and take heed, when they have turned away from such a Messenger and disregarded him, and claimed that he is "one taught (by others), a madman"? As for His saying ﴿taught﴾, it means: he was taught by Jabr, the slave of Ibn al-Hadrami, and by 'Addas, and we have mentioned this before.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: (Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little.) That is: by the supplication of the Prophet. The punishment is the smoke and the famine that we mentioned. And His saying: ﴿a little﴾ means: a short period.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, you will return.﴾ That is: you will return to disbelief. It was also said: you will proceed to the punishment, which is the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 44, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the day We shall seize with the greatest seizing﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions. The first is that it is the day of Badr, and "the greatest seizing" is by capture and killing. The other opinion is that it is the Day of Resurrection, and this is the more sound (aṣaḥḥ).

His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution﴾, that is, We will take retribution by punishment against the disbelievers.

Allah's saying: ﴿And We had already tried before them the people of Pharaoh﴾, meaning: We tested them.

And His saying: ﴿and there came to them a noble Messenger﴾, meaning: noble in the sight of Allah. It is also said: noble, meaning: good in character, and he is Musa (peace be upon him).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That you deliver to me the servants of Allah﴾. Its meaning is: send with me the servants of Allah, meaning the Children of Israel. It was also said that its meaning is: ﴿Deliver to the servants of Allah﴾, that is, "O servants of Allah," as if he said: respond to me and obey me, O servants of Allah. This is the meaning of the first.

And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾, that is, one who possesses trustworthiness. And on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (رضي الله عنه)

Wa-an-la ta'lū 'alā 'ibād Allāh: that is, do not be arrogant, and do not transgress by denial and rejection.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, I have come to you with a clear authority﴾ — that is, with a manifest proof.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord﴾, meaning: I have taken refuge in my Lord and your Lord, and sought protection in Him.

And His saying: ﴿lest you stone me﴾, meaning: lest you kill me. They had threatened him with death. It has also been said that ﴿lest you stone me﴾ means: lest you revile me. The first opinion is preferable, because they reached him by reviling, for attributing him to sorcery and lying is the greatest form of reviling, but they did not reach him by killing.
His saying, Most High: ﴿And if you do not believe me﴾, i.e., do not confirm me, ﴿then leave me alone﴾, i.e., withdraw from me, and be neutral, neither for me nor against me.
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then he called upon his Lord, "These are a criminal people."﴾ That is, polytheists.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 23:

The Exalted said: ﴿So travel with My servants by night﴾, meaning: God the Exalted revealed to him that he should travel with My servants ﴿by night﴾, that is, at night.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾, meaning: that Pharaoh and his army will pursue you.

The Exalted said: ﴿And leave the sea parted (rahwan)﴾. Regarding His saying ﴿rahwan﴾ there are several opinions: first, still/calm; second, dry; third, a path; fourth, smooth and level ground. And the poet said:

(They walk with ease (rahwan), so the rear does not overtake the front, nor do the chests lean upon the rears.)

In the narrative: when Moses crossed the sea, he turned back toward the sea intending to strike it with his staff so that it would return to what it had been, and God the Exalted revealed to him—

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 24:

: ﴿And leave the sea at rest﴾. That is: still (sākinan).

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, they are an army to be drowned﴾. That is: Pharaoh and his people. It is narrated that the army of Pharaoh numbered seven thousand thousand men, and the army of Moses six hundred thousand and a fraction (nayf). It is also said: one thousand and six hundred thousand. And Allah knows best.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on Surah 44, verse 25:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿How many gardens they left behind﴾. That is: orchards (basatin). It was also said: from al-Fayyum to Damietta and Alexandria there were continuous orchards.

And His saying: ﴿and springs﴾. That is: rivers (anhar).

And His saying: ﴿And crops﴾, meaning: tilled lands.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a noble station﴾, meaning: goodly dwellings. It is also said: pulpits. And it has been said that Pharaoh had ordered the making of many pulpits in Egypt so that he might be praised from them.

And His saying: ﴿And luxury in which they had been delighting﴾, meaning: enjoying comfort. It is recited also as "fakihin," meaning "delighted/pleased." And "ni'mah" (blessing, luxury) is that by which one enjoys comfort.

Almost - the verse is 44:28, and the passage is a short tafsir note on it.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Thus. And We made other people inherit them﴾, meaning: the Children of Israel. In the narrative: when God, may He be exalted, drowned Pharaoh and his people, the Children of Israel returned to Egypt, and they settled in the dwellings of the family of Pharaoh and occupied them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾, has several interpretations. The first: what Anas reported, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is not a Muslim except that he has two doors in the heaven: a door through which his deeds ascend, and a door through which his provision descends. When he dies, they both weep for him." Then he recited His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾.

It is also reported from Mujahid that he said: When the Muslim servant dies, his place of prayer weeps for him for forty mornings. In a report from ʿAli (raḍiya Allahu ʿanhu), that when the Muslim servant dies, the place where he used to pray weeps for him, and the door through which his deeds used to ascend [weeps for him].

Abu Yahya said: I said to Mujahid: How can the heaven and the earth weep? He said: Does the earth not weep for one who populates it with bowing and prostration, and does the heaven not weep for a believer whose righteous deed ascends to it?

It is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾, meaning: the people of the heaven and the earth, like His saying, may He be exalted: {And ask the town} (ʿal-qarya), meaning: the people of the town.

It is reported from some of them that the weeping of the heaven is the reddening of its edges. And it is reported from some of the Successors (tabiʿun) that when al-Husayn ibn ʿAli (raḍiya Allahu ʿanhuma) was killed, the edges of the heaven turned red for forty mornings, and that was due to its weeping for him.

It is also reported from some of them that the meaning of the weeping of the heaven and the earth here is that, if they were among those who weep, they would not have wept over the disbeliever, because they know the intensity of God's anger against him.

The most well-known of these opinions is the first, and it is what has been transmitted from the early generations (al-salaf). Some of them said: The weeping of the heavens and the earth is mentioned only because the Arabs say such things about a great calamity. They say: "The sun eclipsed at so-and-so's death, and the sky wept for him." The poet said:

(So the sun is eclipsed, not rising, weeping over you, and the stars of the night and the moon.)

His saying: ﴿and they were not given respite﴾ means: they were not delayed or granted time.

Almighty God says: ﴿And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment﴾. In the explanation (of this verse): Pharaoh used to belittle the Children of Israel and subjugate them, whereas Israel and his descendants held a great station with God, exalted be He.
"And His saying: ﴿From Pharaoh. Indeed he was haughty, among the extravagant.﴾ That is: a tyrant, arrogant, among the polytheists."

"The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We chose them knowingly above the worlds﴾ means: We chose them with Our knowledge of them. His saying ﴿above the worlds﴾ means: above the worlds of their own time. It is also said: above all the worlds, because He singled them out with a great number of prophets from among them, so they have virtue over all the worlds in this sense. The well-known view is the first."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 44, verse 33:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We gave them of the signs that which contained a clear trial.﴾ The signs are such as: the splitting of the sea (firq al-bahr), the drowning of Pharaoh (inhiraq Fir'awn), the deliverance of Musa (Moses) and those with him, the sending down of the manna and the quail, and other signs besides these. His words ﴿that which contained a clear trial (bala' mubin)﴾ mean: a fine blessing (ni'mah hasanah). The Arabs say: "So-and-so has a fine trial (bala' hasan) with me," meaning a fine blessing.

In the story: Pharaoh used to employ the strong among the Children of Israel in labour, until their chests and backs were worn raw from carrying stones, and he slaughtered their sons and spared their women, and he made the women work at spinning and weaving, and similar things. He also imposed on the weak among the Children of Israel a tax on each one of them, which they paid every day. The Copt would come to the Israelite and make him labour at whatever he wished, and when noon came he would release him, saying: "Go and earn what you eat," and he would not give him anything to eat. So God the Exalted delivered them from these afflictions.
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, these ones are saying﴾ — meaning: the polytheists of Mmakkah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 35:

And His saying: ﴿It is not but our first death﴾ means: We die once and are not resurrected after that.

And His saying: ﴿And we will not be raised up﴾ means: not resurrected (mab'uthin). The poet said: (O family of Bakr, revive Kulayb for me... O family of Bakr, where, where is the flight?)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 36:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then bring us our fathers, if you are truthful.﴾ The people of tafsir said: Abu Jahl said: "O Muhammad, resurrect for us some of our fathers, and let Qusay ibn Kilab be among them, for he was an elderly man of truthfulness."

It is also narrated that they asked him to bring back to life for them Lu'ay ibn Ghalib, Murrah ibn Ka'b, and Qusay ibn Kilab.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 37:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Are they better, or the people of Tubba'?﴾ He means: are they more powerful and greater in blessing, or the people of Tubba' (Tubba')? In some reports it is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not revile Tubba', for he had indeed embraced Islam."

It is also related from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that Tubba' was a Muslim. The tubbaʿah (tubba'ah, the kings of Yemen bearing this title) were among the kings of Yemen as the Caesars (qayasirah) were among the kings of Rome, and the Chosroes (akasirah) among the kings of the non-Arabs ('ajam).

In the narrative: Tubba' went out to Iraq and made al-Hirah (al-Hirah) a place of settlement, and he campaigned against China, and he is the one who destroyed the fortress of Samarqand. Those who said that Tubba' had embraced Islam argued that Allah, may He be exalted, censured the people of Tubba' but did not censure Tubba' himself. In the narrative, his conversion to Islam was at the hands of the Jews, and those Jews were upon the truth.

As for His saying: ﴿And those before them, We destroyed them; indeed, they were criminals﴾, He means: possessors of crime (dhu jurm).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.﴾ That is: playing (ʿabithīn), without purpose.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not create them except with truth﴾ means: for the great reward and the great punishment. What is meant by "them" is the people of the heavens and the earth.

And His saying: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾.

Almighty Allah says: ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgment is the appointed time for them all﴾. He means: the Day of Resurrection, on which judgment is made between the creatures, that is, He decides (between them). And it is said: on it He decides between a person and his deeds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 41:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿The Day when no protector (mawla) will avail a protégé (mawla) at all﴾. That is: a close relative will not avail a close relative at all. Its meaning is that the believer will not support his disbelieving relative. It is also said: the believer does not take a disbelieving person as his protector (tawalla) because of kinship with him. From this is the saying of the Prophet: "Whoever I am his mawla (mawla), then ʿAli is his mawla," meaning: whoever I am his protector (walī) by way of love (mahabba) and support (nusra) from the mu'ala (mutual allegiance), then ʿAli is his mawla. It is also said that the report came about on a specific occasion: ʿAli said to Usama, may Allah be pleased with him, "You are my mawla," and Usama said, "I am not your mawla; rather, I am the mawla of the Messenger of Allah." So the Messenger of Allah said: "Whoever I am his mawla, then ʿAli is his mawla."

And His saying: ﴿will avail﴾ means: will not repel (yadfa').

And His saying: ﴿nor will they be helped﴾ means: they will not be defended from the punishment.

Almost all of this passage is commentary on the verse, so I render it as written.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Except for those upon whom Allah has mercy﴾. He means: the believers intercede for one another and take one another as allies (mawla), so intercession is the benefit of allegiance (al-muwalah).

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is the Almighty (al-'Aziz), the Most Merciful (al-Rahim)﴾. That is: the Invincible (al-mani') in His dominion, the Merciful to His creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 43–44:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the sinful one﴾. That is, the wicked (al-fajir). It was said: the disbeliever (al-kafir), and according to the view of most of the exegetes this is Abu Jahl. The meaning of zaqqum has already been explained. It is narrated that the polytheists came to Abu Jahl and said to him: "Muhammad has threatened us with zaqqum; do you know what zaqqum is?" He said: "By God, when you swallow it, it makes you choke; it is al-sarfan with butter, a type of good dates."

Know that zaqqum in the language (lughah) is every food that is eaten with great reluctance. Some of them said: zaqqum is "the soft food" (al-ta'am al-layyin) in the language of the Berbers, not in the language of the Arabs.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 43–44:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the sinful one﴾. That is, the wicked (al-fajir). It was said: the disbeliever (al-kafir), and according to the view of most of the exegetes this is Abu Jahl. The meaning of zaqqum has already been explained. It is narrated that the polytheists came to Abu Jahl and said to him: "Muhammad has threatened us with zaqqum; do you know what zaqqum is?" He said: "By God, when you swallow it, it makes you choke; it is al-sarfan with butter, a type of good dates."

Know that zaqqum in the language (lughah) is every food that is eaten with great reluctance. Some of them said: zaqqum is "the soft food" (al-ta'am al-layyin) in the language of the Berbers, not in the language of the Arabs.

al-Sam'ani's commentary (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 45:

And His saying: ﴿like molten brass (al-muhl)﴾ is the dregs of oil (ikr al-zayt). It was also said: the dregs of tar (qatran). It was also said: molten silver.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It boils in the bellies like the boiling of scalding water﴾. That is: the molten brass boils in the bellies. It was also said: the people (boil) in the bellies, and this is the more correct view.
"And His saying: ﴿like the boiling of scalding water﴾, i.e., like the boiling of water that has reached its extreme heat."

Her is the translation of the passage:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Seize him and drag him﴾ mean: drag him along. It is also said: drive him violently.

And His words: ﴿into the midst of the Blazing Fire﴾ mean: into the middle of the Blazing Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 48:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then pour over his head some of the torment of boiling water﴾. In the tafsir (exegesis) it is said: it is pierced through the middle of Abu Jahl's head, and boiling water is poured into it, so that his intestines come out from its lower part.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 49:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble.﴾ That is: it is said to him, "Taste!" And His words: ﴿the mighty, the noble⦆ mean: in your own opinion. He used to say, "I am the most mighty and most noble of the people of the valley (al-Wadi)." It is also said: "Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble" means: you are neither mighty nor noble. It has also been said: this is said to him in a mocking manner.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on Surah 44, verse 50:

"His words: ﴿Indeed, this is what you used to doubt﴾ means: you used to be in doubt."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place﴾. That is, in an abode where they will be safe from death and from ceasing to exist. ʿAli said: "They will be made safe from death, so life became pleasant for them."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verses 52–53:

And His saying: ﴿In gardens and springs, they will wear [garments] of fine silk and brocade, facing one another⟩ — meaning: the fine part of brocade (dībāj). It was also said: it is khazz (silk) that is patterned (mūshā).

And His saying: ﴿And thick silk brocade⟩ — meaning: the thick brocade (dībāj). It is said: istabraq is brocade that is raised (murtafi') and has a sheen (barīq) in the eyes.

And His saying: ﴿Facing one another⟩ — meaning: no one looks at the back of another's neck. It was also said: "facing one another" in love, not turning their backs on one another in enmity.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verses 52–53:

And His saying: ﴿In gardens and springs, they will wear [garments] of fine silk and brocade, facing one another⟩ — meaning: the fine part of brocade (dībāj). It was also said: it is khazz (silk) that is patterned (mūshā).

And His saying: ﴿And thick silk brocade⟩ — meaning: the thick brocade (dībāj). It is said: istabraq is brocade that is raised (murtafi') and has a sheen (barīq) in the eyes.

And His saying: ﴿Facing one another⟩ — meaning: no one looks at the back of another's neck. It was also said: "facing one another" in love, not turning their backs on one another in enmity.

"The saying of Him, the Exalted: ﴿Thus, and We shall wed them to ḥūr ʿīn﴾ (ḥūr ʿīn). That is: just as We did to them what We have mentioned, thus We shall wed them to the ḥūr ʿīn. The ḥūr (ḥūr) are the fair, pure-white maidens, and the ʿīn (ʿīn) are those with beautiful, large eyes. It is also said: they are named ḥūr because the eyes are dazzled (taḥār) by their beauty. Ibn Masʿūd recited: "[wa-ʿays] ʿīn" (wa-ʿays ʿīn), meaning: the white ones."

Al-Sam'ani's words on the verse: "They call for every kind of fruit therein, secure." (Qur'an 44:55)

Here the meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 56:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They taste therein no death, except the first death﴾. That is, apart from the first death. The first death does not occur in Paradise; He spoke in this manner by way of extension (tawassu'). It has also been said: this is an exceptive clause of disjunction (istithna' munqati'), and its meaning is: "But the first death, they have already tasted it."

And His saying: ﴿And He has protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾. That is, the punishment of the Fire, and al-Jahim (the Blazing Fire) is the greatest part of the Fire.
Allah's saying: ﴿As a bounty from your Lord﴾, i.e., as a favour (tafaddul) from your Lord. ﴿That is the supreme triumph﴾, i.e., the great salvation.

The Exalted said: ﴿So indeed, We have made it easy with your tongue﴾. Meaning: We made the Qur'an easy with your tongue. It is also said: We loosened your tongue with it. This has the same meaning as His words: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance ...﴾ the verse.

And His words: ﴿so that they may remember﴾. Meaning: that they may admonish themselves.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 44, verse 59:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿So watch, [O Muhammad], and they too are watching﴾. That is: await their punishment and expect it, for they too are awaiting [what will befall them].
